==English==

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂er-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|article}}, from {{der|en|fro|article}}, from {{der|en|la|articulus|t=a joint, limb, member, part, division, the article in grammar, a point of time}}, from {{der|en|la|artus}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂értus||that which is fit together; juncture, ordering}}, from the root {{m|ine-pro|*h₂er-||to join, fit (together)}}. {{doublet|en|articulus}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɑːtɪkl̩/|[ˈɑːtʰɪkʰəɫ]|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɑɹtɪkəl/|/ˈɑɹtəkl̩/|[ˈɑ(ː)ɹɾɨkɫ̩]|a=GA}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-article.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɑː(ɹ)tɪkəl|s=3}}

===Noun===
{{wp|+ (publishing)}}
{{wp|+ (grammar)}}
{{en-noun}}

# A piece of [[nonfiction]] [[writing]] such as a [[story]], [[report]], opinion piece, or [[entry]] in a newspaper, magazine, journal, encyclopedia, etc.
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2012-03| author=Lee A. Groat| volume=100| issue=2| page=128| magazine=w:American Scientist| title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/feature/2012/2/gemstones Gemstones]| passage=Although there are dozens of different types of gems, among the best known and most important are {{...}}. (Common gem materials not addressed in this '''article''' include amber, amethyst, chalcedony, garnet, lazurite, malachite, opals, peridot, rhodonite, spinel, tourmaline, turquoise and zircon.)}}
# An [[object]], a [[member]] of a [[group]] or [[class]].
#: {{co|en|an '''article''' of clothing}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=12|passage=There were many wooden chairs for the bulk of his visitors, and two wicker armchairs with red cloth cushions for superior people. From the packing-cases had emerged some Indian clubs,{{nb...}}, and all these '''articles'''{{nb...}} made a scattered and untidy decoration that Mrs. Clough assiduously dusted and greatly cherished.}}
#* {{RQ:Bramah Eyes of Max Carrados|passage=Had he bought nitre before, I have since tried to recall and I cannot. It is a common enough '''article''' and I sell it every day.}}
# {{senseid|en|Q103184}}{{lb|en|grammar}} A [[part of speech]] that indicates, specifies and limits a noun (''a'', ''an'', or ''the'' in English). In some languages the '''article''' may appear as an ending (e.g. definite '''article''' in Swedish) or there may be none (e.g. Russian, Pashto).
# A [[section]] of a [[legal]] document, [[bylaw]]s, etc. or, in the plural, the entire document seen as a collection of these.
#: {{ux|en|The [[w:Articles of War|'''Articles''' of War]] are a set of regulations{{...}}to govern the conduct of{{...}}military{{...}}forces}}
# {{ellipsis of|en|genuine article}}. {{rfex|en}}
# A [[part]] or [[segment]] of something joined to other parts, or, in [[combination]], forming a [[structured]] [[set]].
#: {{ux|en|Each of the [[w:Solifugae|chelicerae]] is composed of two '''articles''', forming a powerful pincer.}}
#* {{RQ:Paley Principles of Moral and Political Philosophy|text=upon each '''article''' of human duty}}
#* {{RQ:Erasmus Darwin Zoonomia|text=the different '''articles''' which compose the blood}}
# {{lb|en|derogatory|dated}} A [[person]]; an individual.
#: {{co|en|a shrewd '''article'''}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete|slang}} A [[wench]].
#: {{ux|en|She's a prime '''article''', a devilish good piece, a hell of a goer.}}
# {{lb|en|dated}} Subject matter; concern.
#* {{RQ:Spectator|II|119|17 July 1711|text=a very great revolution that happened in this '''article''' of good breeding}}
#* {{RQ:Defoe Plague Year|text=This last '''article''' perhaps will hardly be believed.}}
# {{lb|en|dated}} A distinct part.
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} A precise point in time; a moment.
#* {{RQ:Evelyn Diary|13 July 1683|text=This fatal news coming to Hick's Hall upon the '''article''' of my Lord Russell's trial, was said to have had no little influence on the jury and all the bench to his prejudice.}}
#* '''1805''', {{w|Charles Hall (economist)|Charles Hall}}, ''The Effects of Civilisation on the People in European States'', [[s:The Effects of Civilisation on the People in European States/Original Preface|Original Preface]]:
#*: {{...}} who has more opportunities of acquiring the knowledge, than a physician? He is admitted into the dwellings of all ranks of people, and into the innermost parts of them; he sees them by their fireside, at their tables, and in their beds; he sees them at work, and at their recreations; he sees them in health, in sickness, and in the '''article''' of death; {{...}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1634|author=w:William Habington|title=Castara
|passage=each '''article''' of time}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To bind by articles of [[apprenticeship]].
#: {{co|en|to '''article''' an apprentice to a mechanic}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1876|author=Sabine Baring-Gould|title=The Vicar of Morwenstow|chapter=[[s:Of Human Bondage/Chapter LIV|Chapter LIV]]
|passage=When the boy left school at Liskeard, he was '''articled''' to a lawyer, Mr. Jacobson, at Plymouth, a wealthy man in good practice, first cousin to his mother; but this sort of profession did not at all approve itself to Robert's taste, and he only remained with Mr. Jacobson a few months.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1948|month=May and June|title=G. A. Sekon|journal=Railway Magazine|page=145|text=After educational training at Hayes Grammar School and Hayes College, Mr. Nokes was '''articled''' to a Surveyor and Land Agent in 1885, and, at the expiration of his articles, became a partner in the firm.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To accuse or charge by an exhibition of articles or accusations.
#* {{RQ:Pepys Diary|volume=IV|date=25 March 1665|page=381|text=At noon dined alone with Sir W. Batten, where great discourse of Sir W. Pen, Sir W. Batten being, I perceive, quite out of love with him, thinking him too great and too high, and began to talk that the world do question his courage, upon which I told him plainly I have been told that he was '''articled''' against for it, and that Sir H. Vane was his great friend therein.}}
#*: {{...}}if the Captain of any Merchant ship under convoy shall wilfully disobey Signals{{...}}he shall be liable to be '''articled''' against in the High Court of Admiralty{{...}}
# To formulate in articles; to set forth in distinct particulars.
#* {{RQ:Taylor Holy Living|passage=If {{...}}all his errors and follies were '''articled''' against him, the man would seem vicious and miserable.}}
